afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 162225
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
325 PM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Warm and dry conditions today will give way to a cold frontal 
  passage Tuesday yielding slightly below normal temperatures the 
  remainder of the week. 

- A weather disturbance moving through the region Tuesday will 
  support chances of showers and locally gusty winds with dry, 
  tranquil weather returning Wednesday. 

- Another weather system entering the region Friday will provide 
  the next chance of rain focused mainly in higher terrain 
  locations.

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Tuesday/...
Objective analysis this afternoon shows increasing southwest flow
between a trough moving into the western CONUS from the Pacific 
and a departing ridge. H5 heights are falling during this
transition, but 850mb temps will remain above normal at 12-14C
with warm southerly flow. This will lead to above normal surface
temperatures this afternoon, with lower deserts reaching highs 
near 80 degrees, under mostly clear to partly clouds skies and 
light winds.

Over the next 36 hours, guidance shows the Pacific trough will
deepen as it moves across central CA and also transition from
neutral orientation to a negative tilt with the vorticity center
lifting northeast through Las Vegas and NW AZ midday tomorrow.
Despite the vorticity mostly missing the local area a cold front
will still be dragged through the area Tuesday and sufficient low
and mid level moisture (PWATs up to 200-250% of normal) will be 
pulled north into the region to support isolated to scattered rain
showers, beginning around or after midnight tonight and lasting
through early to mid afternoon Tuesday. With the cold core mostly
missing the local area, forcing will be limited mostly to 
frontogenetical and upslope. Hi-res and global models continue to
exhibit good agreement showing forecast rainfall amounts likely
staying below <0.50", with anywhere from 0.00" to 0.30" in south-
central AZ. Highest totals will favor northern Maricopa County
into Yavapai County with the upslope element. A few embedded
thunderstorms will still be possible (10-20% chance) with minimal
instability being advertised (100-200 J/kg MUCAPE), but storms
will be handicapped by poor to fair mid-level lapse rates (5.5-6
C/km). Any stronger shower or storm that develops will still be
capable of producing locally higher rainfall amounts and there is
at least a low chance (10%) for isolated rainfall amounts of 1+".
The cold front should rapidly clear the forecast area by Tuesday 
evening with strong subsidence and a weakening pressure gradient 
in its wake.

In addition to the rain chances, gusty winds are expected across
the area Tuesday with S-SW wind gusts up to 20-30 mph anticipated
ahead of the cold front across AZ. In southeast CA, strong
westerly post-frontal winds are expected to develop tonight, with
evidence of 900-800mb winds reaching 30-35 kts. Hi-res guidance
continues to show winds in southwest Imperial County gusting up to
40-45 kts. A Wind Advisory has been issued for this area from
tonight through midday Tuesday. There is some uncertainty in how
strong winds will get in the Imperial Valley. Models have been
showing peak gusts around 30-35 mph, however models are known to
at times underestimate the strength of the winds in the Valley.
Cross-sectional model analysis of wind, omega, and stability
suggest the potential for strong downsloping winds. So, it will
not be surprising if the Valley sees a few gusts peaking up around
40-45 mph, but have held off on including the Valley in the
advisory. Winds of this magnitude will be capable of generating
localized blowing dust/sand channels. Winds will subside across
the region by Tuesday evening.


&&

.LONG TERM /Wednesday through Sunday/...    
Flat ridging/quasi-zonal flow will briefly settle over the SW Conus 
Wednesday before another pronounced trough with strong cyclonic flow 
propagates inland from the East Pacific late in the week. Ensemble 
agreement is excellent maintaining the bulk of the negative height 
anomaly and cold core well into central/northern California and 
Nevada. As such, the jet core should only descend into northern 
Arizona keeping the forecast area under a more anti-cyclonic 
subsident regime. Some moisture may be entrained along a decaying 
cold front Thursday night/Friday, though orographics will likely 
contribute the greatest towards focused ascent. Given this scenario, 
POPs are only highlighted in higher terrain areas with minimal QPF. 
Regardless, this trough passage will reinforce temperatures 3F-6F 
below normal through the weekend with unusually good confidence 
given narrow spread of numerical guidance uncharacteristic for 5 
days in advance during the passage of a weather system. Ensemble 
variations grow substantially late in the weekend due to the 
interaction of Pacific energy with an enhanced subtropical jet. 
While the operational GFS and a handful of GEFS members suggest 
another deepening trough entering the SW Conus, this solution is 
more of a minority versus the entire NAEFS suite with the ensemble 
mean favoring only inconsequential broad cyclonic, or quasi-zonal 
flow towards the end of this forecast period. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1825Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Aviation weather concerns this TAF period will be related to a
cold front expected to move eastward through the Phoenix airspace
Tuesday late morning/early afternoon. Today, expect FEW-SCT cloud
decks AOA 7K ft AGL, winds favoring SE, and possibly some VRB or
light west winds for a few hours around sunset. Winds will revert
to SE tonight and gradually increase through early Tuesday morning
as lower VFR CIGs fill into the area. VCSH conditions may begin as
early as 12Z-14Z coinciding with good confidence in BKN CIGs
between 4-6K ft AGL. Chances for brief MVFR CIGs will be best at
KDVT and KSDL, but are still fairly low, peaking around 30%, so
opted to keep CIGs in a VFR category for now. In future updates,
will likely need to add PROB30/TEMPO groups for -SHRA at all the
terminals (currently only included for PHX). Winds will become
gusty out of the S/SE Tuesday morning ahead of the front and
abruptly shift SW/W behind the front, early Tuesday afternoon. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
Gusty SW to W winds will be the primary aviation concern through
the TAF period under periods of SCT-BKN cloud decks AOA 5-8K ft
AGL. Winds today will remain light, mostly AOB 6 kts and favor SE.
This evening, winds are expected to increase out of the SW, with
moderate confidence in W'rly gusts developing overnight at KIPL.
Gusts are likely to peak between 20-30 kts at KIPL and around
20-25 kts at KBLH on Tuesday. Confidence is too low to include
VCSH/SHRA in the TAF at either site, but the best probabilities 
(10-20%) will be present near KBLH between 06Z-15Z. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry conditions with temperatures slightly above normal today will 
give way to increased rainfall chances and cooler temperatures 
Tuesday. Wetting rain chances Tuesday are around 40-70% over 
upslope areas north and east of Phoenix, while locally gusty winds
affect parts of western districts. Otherwise, minimum afternoon 
humidity levels will fall into a 20-30% range in western districts
and 30-50% across eastern districts. This will follow good to 
excellent overnight recovery of 60-100%. Another weather system 
moving through the region Friday may provide another round of 
rain, but mostly confined to higher terrain north and east of 
Phoenix, while reinforcing cooler temperatures. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least the next couple days due 
to water released from the dam. Water releases remain around 3000 
cfs. This will have the potential to flood farm fields and low water 
crossings along the river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...Wind Advisory from 11 PM this evening to 1 PM PST Tuesday for 
     CAZ562-566.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...18
AVIATION...Whittock
FIRE WEATHER...18
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
